english_verification.review_scope: Read the complete shared A21/Z43 source body and original evidence page; checked A21's current history, the A21 migration mission, representative Aelnar mission branches, and actual English flavour text for faction names, the shared population-removal mission, and Lithiel's living-battery route. Read the actual Wiki Markdown chunks from two pages. Confirmed that Elissa's extreme route is conditional; no exhaustive mission audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Aelnar Wiki page is revision 17057 and provides worldbuilding history rather than a mandatory player timeline; the article does not treat its dated civil-war and downfall account as a required campaign future.

The optional Elissa extreme-magic route is not mandatory; common Z43 purge content and mutually exclusive branch harms remain distinct. No attempt was made to collapse every route into a single playthrough.

rationale.campaign_length: 19 direct A21 missions and 155 Z43 mission definitions; Z43 includes mutually exclusive factions and extra modules, so these do not add up to 174 sequential missions in a single campaign.
rationale.colonization: Exploration, building a colonial nation of sufficient size, and migration are the core loop of the A21 prelude and the route into Z43.
rationale.complexity: The two mission trees, migration requirements, disaster, six political centers, and conditional mission groups are intertwined.
rationale.dark_story: Ethnic purges in shared missions, second-class status on some routes, and living magical batteries on one branch make for an explicitly dark narrative.
rationale.difficulty: A major civil-war penalty, conditional branches, and cross-continental expansion create high management demands; not quantified in an actual playthrough.
rationale.diplomacy: The early game requires Cannorian diplomacy and colonial nations; later, faction politics transform internal relations.
rationale.early_pressure: Early pressure centers on colonial pacing, diplomatic security, and resources for migration; the opening situation can vary.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Elissa and some factions have an extreme frost-magic and living-battery theme; other routes are less intense, so phases are scored separately.
rationale.narrative_density: The ancestral-homeland narrative, transoceanic migration, Rianvisa, and mutually exclusive endings form a long, connected epic.
rationale.tall_play: Colonial settlements, the capital, and industry require development, but the main arc emphasizes migration and conquest.
rationale.trade_economy: Overseas colonization, Noruin trade, and imperial economics support the expedition and civil war.
rationale.warfare: After migration, the country expands across Aelantir; the civil war also brings internal warfare.

identity.appearance: A21 Venáil begins in 1444 as a Moon Elf republic; after transoceanic migration and the formation decision it becomes Z43 Aelnar. Z43's country-history file is a post-formation template, not evidence of 1444 holdings.
identity.formation_scope: Only A21 can form Z43 through the aelnar_nation decision, after securing the Elven Rekindling flag, placing its capital in the Noruin colonial region, being at peace and meeting the eligible independence status, while Z43 does not exist. The effect changes Tag, replaces non-generic missions, raises government rank, and changes ideas. Z69–Z73 and similar claimants in the Rianvisa are rebel factions that may appear, not successor countries formed in sequence.

predecessors.relationship: The sole predecessor eligible to click the current decision forming Z43; has 19 exclusive prologue missions.

successors.relationship: The main campaign after A21 forms it by decision; its 155 mission definitions include mutually exclusive factions.

survey_region.note: The original table's Tag is Venail/Aelnar and maps to the identity of this continuous local campaign: A21 Venáil at the start, later forming Z43 Aelnar. The region is not split into predecessor and successor entries.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Our people are overjoyed at the rediscovery of our homeland. Even now, droves of our kin are preparing to set sail to resettle their ancient motherland- and reclaim what was lost in the ashes of time.
description.text_en: Our people are overjoyed at the rediscovery of our homeland. Even now, droves of our kin are preparing to set sail to resettle their ancient motherland- and reclaim what was lost in the ashes of time.

description.text: The years we spent adrift on the Remnant Fleet were harrowing and brutal, but those who survived were able to teach later generations much in the ways of seafaring. Let us embrace this knowledge and use it to reclaim our home!
description.text_en: The years we spent adrift on the Remnant Fleet were harrowing and brutal, but those who survived were able to teach later generations much in the ways of seafaring. Let us embrace this knowledge and use it to reclaim our home!

description.text: The Day of Ashen Skies was the lowest point in all of elven civilization, which makes the prospect of reversing the doom and reclaiming our home all the more appealing. Our people place their hopes and dreams in Aelantir, and we must do our best to fulfill them.
description.text_en: The Day of Ashen Skies was the lowest point in all of elven civilization, which makes the prospect of reversing the doom and reclaiming our home all the more appealing. Our people place their hopes and dreams in Aelantir, and we must do our best to fulfill them.

description.text: Our people were shocked to discover what became of the elves we left behind. What little sentience these feral beasts retain is consumed entirely by an instinctive hatred for us, their kin - we must put them in their place.
description.text_en: Our people were shocked to discover what became of the elves we left behind. What little sentience these feral beasts retain is consumed entirely by an instinctive hatred for us, their kin - we must put them in their place.

description.text: As the recolonization continues, our shipwrights have developed massive arks that can carry myriads of colonists using only a skeleton crew - let us adapt these developments for the rest of our fleet.
description.text_en: As the recolonization continues, our shipwrights have developed massive arks that can carry myriads of colonists using only a skeleton crew - let us adapt these developments for the rest of our fleet.

description.text: Our colonial ventures are proceeding smoothly, but it has come to our attention that certain resources from Aelantir could be... better allocated. Let us charge a small tariff on goods from Aelantir to help cover our rising operational costs. I'm sure they won't mind...
description.text_en: Our colonial ventures are proceeding smoothly, but it has come to our attention that certain resources from Aelantir could be... better allocated. Let us charge a small tariff on goods from Aelantir to help cover our rising operational costs. I'm sure they won't mind...

description.text: Thanks to the nautical advances pioneered for the trips to Aelantir, our vessels are now able to sail anywhere across the globe, allowing our diaspora to venture to the farthest reaches of the land. This may prove useful in building a truly global trade network...

description.text: Established during the overhaul of Aelnar's naval doctrines, the Teal Armada is a maritime body composed solely of heavy vessels with a sky-colored bow, whose main function is to protect Aelnar coastline.

description.text: Written by Nesterin Lufaren, 'Pulsar Economics' is a book describing a series of economic concepts whose purpose is the creation of a 'body' of worker specializing in the production of a particular good.

description.text: Alariandel, who left us in the year 1512, is still recognized today as the greatest navigator to have emerged in the country. Even today, her ideas and doctrines shape the imagination of many children, and the charts of many ships.

description.text: With no claws, no fur, no thick leather, no sharp teeth, it is necessary for each elf to engrave in him the fundamentals of the most recent military tactics if he want to survive on the battlefield. In order to ensure that such an idea is implemented, the establishment of Military Academy throughout the country has been a priority maintained throughout all the history of Aelnar.

description.text: 'A stable society is a homogeneous society'. It was with these words that the first plans for a program to maintain ethnic purity within each position of power were created. But in order to leave no talent aside, it is necessary that from birth, the future talents of the country are ethnically clean.

description.text: Invented by Kayd's only daughter, the Dalanai Rifle is a revolutionary rifle that quickly proved its worth. These rifles were sometimes elaborately carved and decorated with finely etched brass or silver plates. But the rifle's most critical quality was its extended barrel that featured twisting grooves along the interior bore. These grooves guided a lead ball or other projectile to spin as it exited the barrel, ensuring a straighter line shot and better aim for the gunner.

description.text: Our empire is great, our empire is vast, and our fleet is the backbone of everything. In order to never let this giant crumble on itself, our ships will sail through every sea, every ocean, every river of Aelantir, like the blood of a giant.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want peaceful development, do not want a major civil-war disaster, or do not want explicit ethnic-purge and living-exploitation narratives.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Colonize and prepare to migrate early; expand widely and consolidate the state after formation; then survive the Rianvisa and follow the winning faction's missions.
player_overview.overview: Start in Cannor as Venáil, explore and colonize Aelantir, and organize a mass migration to Noruin to qualify to form Aelnar. The huge new-continent mission tree then pushes conquest and state-building toward the Rianvisa: multiple leaders contest the empire's future, and some victors unlock unique routes. It is a grand colonial and civil-war epic, but includes ethnic purges in shared missions and living magical exploitation on a specific branch; one campaign cannot experience every ending.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy transoceanic migration, an exceptionally long colonial war, civil war, and multi-faction political stories.
signature_features: The Venáil prologue uses colonial-nation size and migration missions to move Old World resources and the capital to Aelantir.
The Aelnari Rianvisa pits multiple claimants against one another and switches between mutually exclusive mission groups.
Ethnic purges in the shared main line and magical exploitation on some branches give the revival ideal a clearly dark cost.
player_overview.tagline: Lead the Moon Elves across the sea to a new homeland, then decide what kind of country the Star Elf Empire will become.

reasons: A transoceanic migration prelude with real resource costs.
The Rianvisa and its rival leaders give the post-formation country multiple political endings.
Colonization, imperial war, and an extreme magical route form a large-scale epic.
warnings: A21 must complete its missions and migration conditions before forming Z43.
The Rianvisa severely harms the economy, colonization, and stability.
Shared missions contain explicit ethnic purges; some branches go further.

phase_scores.phase: Aelnar's formation and Star Elf supremacy
Shared purge missions and extreme succession branches

positive_indicators: Venáil's early voyage and vision of rebuilding its community.
Some succession routes treat non-Star Elves relatively less harshly.
New-continent infrastructure and political integration offer limited public benefit.
values.rationale: Colonization, conquest, migration, and monarchy are not penalized in themselves. The current shared mission group visible to all Z43 factions explicitly calls for eliminating the local population, changes its culture, and applies a modifier named aelnar_genocide; the Dahvar route calls for purging multiple peoples, while the Lithiel-to-Elissa route includes second-class status and using Ruinborn Elves as living magical batteries. Early A21 is not equivalent to the later regime, and some leaders are relatively moderate, so the assessment uses phase scores and medium confidence. Atrocities from mutually exclusive paths cannot be added together and presented as mandatory in one campaign.
red_flags: The shared mission explicitly calls for eliminating the local population and replacing it with Star Elves.
Mission effects forcibly change culture and apply the aelnar_genocide modifier.
Some factions call for mass purges, second-class status, or magical batteries.
